svg.aria-label: Diagram: Microsoft Entra entitlement management structure and the external user lifecycle. A catalog is a container of related resources and access packages used for delegation, where an administrator can add resources to any catalog but a non-administrator can only add resources they own, and a catalog creator automatically becomes the owner of a catalog they create. An access package is a bundle of resources always contained in a catalog, and carries one or more policies; a single access package can have one policy for employees to request access and a second for external identities. Resources that can be bundled are Microsoft Entra security group membership, Microsoft 365 Groups and Teams membership, enterprise application assignment, SharePoint Online site membership, API permissions for agent identities in preview, and SAP IAG business roles in preview. Indirectly this reaches Microsoft 365 licences through group-based licensing, Azure resource access through an Azure role assignment on a group, and Microsoft Entra roles through role-assignable groups. The external user lifecycle runs: add a connected organization, ensure the catalog is enabled for external users, create an access package with a policy for identities not in your directory, decide whether the package is hidden, send a My Access link to a sponsor at the partner, the external user requests, an approver approves, a B2B guest account is created without sending an email, resources are assigned, and on expiry the access is removed and the account is blocked and then deleted. By default the account is blocked from signing in and removed after 30 days, configurable to zero days for immediate removal, and the three settings are Remove external user, Block external user from signing in, and Number of days before removal. Entitlement management only removes accounts it invited itself or ones explicitly converted to governed, so a guest who already existed in the directory before receiving an assignment will remain. There is no notification when an account is removed, only when the access package expires. Prerequisites that must be relaxed or configured include removing or updating B2B allow and blocklists which take precedence, enabling email one-time passcode for an All users policy, setting SharePoint organization-level external sharing to Anyone or New and existing guests, and excluding the Entitlement Management app and the Request Approvals Read Platform from Conditional Access policies affecting guests, since guests have no registered device and no known location. Licensing requires Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra Suite.
svg.title: Access packages convert a standing fact into an event with an expiry date
svg.text: A guest is a standing fact somebody must remember. An assignment is an event with an expiry.
“When their access expires, if they have no other access package assignments, their B2B account… can be automatically removed.”
Three objects, and the delegation is the point of two of them
CATALOG
container for delegation. A creator automatically becomes its owner, and
“a nonadministrator can only add… the resources that they own”
ACCESS PACKAGE
the bundle of resources a project needs — always inside a catalog
POLICY
who may request · who approves · how long before it expires.
One package can carry several — one for staff, one for the partner.
So the resource bundle is defined once and the guardrails vary by who is asking. Policies need not involve a request at all:
assignment can follow “identity properties like department or cost center” — and “remove… access when those properties change”.
What a group gets you, indirectly
Security group + group-based licensing
→ Microsoft 365 licences, requestable and expiring
Security group + an Azure role assignment
→ access to manage Azure resources
Role-assignable group + an Entra role
→ a directory role, bypassing PIM’s activation model
Prefer PIM for roles; packages for what roles touch.
You never need the partner’s staff list
Invite one contact, designate them a sponsor, and make
sponsors the approvers — “they’re likely to know which
external users from their organization need access.”
Send them a My Access link; they distribute it.
Two defaults to check: a new catalog is already “Enabled
for external users”, and an unhidden package is browsable
in My Access by anyone the policy allows.
End of life: three settings, and two of them bite
Default on losing a last assignment
blocked from signing in, then removed after 30 days
Immediate removal
set “Number of days before removing” to 0
Blocking sign-in
they are “unable to re-request” — bad for staff who cycle on and off
Reversing the setting later
already-scheduled deletions “still be deleted on their original schedule”
Notification on removal
none. Expiry is notified; deletion is silent.
And the limit that decides what to promise: it governs only what it created. “If the guest was present in this directory prior
to receiving access package assignments, they’ll remain.” Switching this on stops the problem growing; it does not clean up.
The better-designed half: a governed guest later added to a SharePoint site by hand is “still be removed”. Governance wins.
Switching it on means re-deciding defences you already put up
A B2B allow-list or blocklist
“takes precedence” — governed invitation is blocked until it is updated
An “All users” policy
needs email one-time passcode first, and auto-creates connected orgs
CA requiring device or location
exclude the Entitlement Management app, or guests cannot reach My Access
CA blocking all cloud apps
also exclude Request Approvals Read Platform — via a custom attribute filter
SharePoint external sharing
must be Anyone or New and existing guests for sites to be includable
The pattern worth copying: do not relax a control, NARROW it. Set SharePoint sharing to “Existing guests” and “only new users
that are invited through entitlement management are able to gain access to these sites.” The governed path becomes the only path.
Licence: Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Entra Suite — above P2. And per post #54, none of it exists in an external tenant.
Sources: What is entitlement management?, and Govern access for external users in entitlement management, on Microsoft Learn.
